name: Lizard2-Flat-v1

command.why: The recipe samples 0-3 m/s on the framework's own 10 s window, so the protocol declares a BOX and the record carries the command actually issued each frame -- a range in the yaml and the tensor the manager issues are two things the config alone cannot tell apart. The top of the window carries headroom past the retired lizard line's 3.0 m/s by owner decision (2026-09-22), so 'it cannot reach 3 m/s' must not be read as a policy failure before the actuator reading says so.

why_v1: One mean cannot judge a range command: a run that walks in [0.1, 1.0) and stalls in [2.0, 3.0] and a run that is uniformly mediocre produce the same mean and are different failures. So the bands are part of the criterion (tracking_banded_v1 / displacement_banded_v1) and every band must pass, including the zero-command band, which is read in absolute units and in the criterion rather than left out as 'the command is rarely zero'.

The zero band is a declared band, not a special case: bands partition the command window ([0.0, 0.1) and then the three relative bands), so a frame belongs to exactly one of them, and a frame outside every band is a declaration hole the judge fails on instead of dropping.

The old normalized comparison is not reused. `tracking_v1.normalized` divides by `max(v_cmd, 1e-6)`, which turns a near-zero command into noise, and `displacement_v1.normalized` divides per env before averaging, which is unstable as the expected distance approaches zero. `floor_mps` and 'sum over the band first, divide after' replace both.

The four criteria the retired families' protocols do not have are added as new kinds with their own judge id (`judge`: baseline-criteria-banded-1) rather than by editing a published kind: a changed criterion has to be a new name, or old records would silently point at a reader that no longer exists.

A gate here is a pass condition, not a diagnostic. `non_foot_carrier_v1` and `non_foot_load_sum_v1` are both required: the first collapses the bodies before the dwell (bodies taking turns carrying), the second sums them first (two bodies under the fraction carrying the weight between them). Their thresholds are breach LEVELS -- raising one is looser, and both sit above the measured healthy reading and below the retired line's measured failure (11.6-12.8% of body weight) by construction, not at it.

No lift term in the gait criterion. The record carries per-foot contact and load, not height, and a threshold on a quantity the run never measured is refused everywhere else in this module; the criterion therefore reads swing duration and the load recovered on landing, and the support-phase drag it cannot see stays a report-only number.
